stem: A phentermine prescription is four months old with four completed refills. Select all supported statements.

choices.text: A fifth refill may remain within the federal numerical limit.
The prescription remains refillable for one year.
Covered Schedule IV dispensing is MassPAT-reportable.
Phentermine is Schedule II and cannot be refilled.
The drug is omitted from MassPAT because it is used for weight loss.

explanation.core_reasoning: Apply each proposition independently. A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner. Covered pharmacies report dispensing of Schedule II through V controlled substances and DPH-designated additional drugs, including gabapentin, to the Massachusetts PMP under the current submission standard. phentermine (Adipex-P) is used for short-term adjunct in a weight-reduction regimen. It is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV; its legal consequence in this scenario follows the cited schedule-specific rule.

choice_analysis.B: This statement imports Schedule II prescriptions may not be refilled without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
choice_analysis.C: The proposition 'Covered Schedule IV dispensing is MassPAT-reportable.' is supported by Massachusetts pharmacy MassPAT dispensing-data reporting: Covered pharmacies report dispensing of Schedule II through V controlled substances and DPH-designated additional drugs, including gabapentin, to the Massachusetts PMP under the current submission standard.
choice_analysis.D: This statement imports Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription-drug status without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
choice_analysis.E: This statement imports Schedule II partial fill caused by pharmacy inability without its required trigger and is not supported by the scenario.
